extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and wire-service editors (AP audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and producing hard-news wire copy (international and domestic) suitable for distribution by a news agency; includes handling factual detail, official statements, and procedural reporting. Emphasis on concise, attributable factual reporting for editors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for classifying a 'security risk'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'security risk' may be a person who is talkative about secret or confidential matters after he's had a couple of drinks; someone who is absent-minded; a consistent violator of routine security regulations regarding safeguarding important documents; a person who deliberately associates with known subversives; a person whose behavior places him in a position where he might yield to blackmail or pressure to obtain unauthorized information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists multiple illustrative examples and circumstances that can make a person a security risk: absent-minded clerks or officials, habitual violators of security rules, those who associate with known subversives, or those vulnerable to blackmail. These examples are presented as grounds for classifying someone as a security risk even if their loyalty is not otherwise questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/indicator of a 'disloyal person'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'disloyal person' is one who places the interest of another country (or organization) above that of the United States; could be a paid agent of another government or an individual who acts to serve a foreign authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article distinguishes disloyalty from mere security risk: disloyalty implies placing another country's interest above the U.S. or being an agent of another government. This serves as a higher-level criterion used by officials when evaluating personnel for security or loyalty concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: AEC decision-making standard: eliminate hazard while preserving historical values
rubrics_metrics.description: The Atomic Energy Commission (AEC) states an obligation 'for elimination of this hazard' at the Alamogordo (bomb crater) site but also pledges to 'hold up the progress of the work long enough to discuss ... ways and means of carrying it out which will provide the necessary health protection while preserving as much as possible of the historical exhibition values of the site.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets a two-part standard for action: (1) protect public health by eliminating potential hazards at an atomic test site; and (2) simultaneously seek approaches that conserve the site's historic/exhibition value. The AEC indicated it will delay physical work until representatives can discuss and propose methods that balance safety and preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement policy for demonstrations at Senate hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectators were warned that no demonstration would be allowed in the small committee room; Capitol police were called and instructed to arrest anyone who participated in any demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes a procedural enforcement standard used during crowded committee hearings: proactive warnings to spectators and the explicit instruction to police to arrest demonstrators. It functions as a clear operational rule for maintaining order at hearings.
